result: In dermal fibroblasts from an APDS2 patient, there was no increased PI3K signaling (measured by AKT phosphorylation), p110δ expression was markedly reduced, and p110α levels were unchanged. The truncated p85α ΔEx11 was expressed at much lower levels than wild-type p85α.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly confirmed these findings. Reviewer 1 states the study 'provides convincing data showing that expression of the PIK3R1(deltaExon11) dominant negative mutation in APDS1/2 patient-derived cells reduces AKT activation and p110δ protein levels.' Reviewer 2 similarly notes 'They found no evidence of hyperactive PI3K signalling monitored by pAKT in a APDS2 patient-derived dermal fibroblast cells' and confirms 'p110 delta protein levels were strongly reduced.'

result: In 3T3-L1 preadipocytes, overexpression of the APDS2 ΔEx11 p85α variant did not increase basal PI3Kα signaling but potently inhibited insulin-induced Akt phosphorylation, demonstrating dominant negative activity. The variant associates with Irs1 and Irs2 but fails to heterodimerize with p110α. Overexpression severely impaired adipocyte differentiation, similar to SHORT syndrome variants.
evaluation: Reviewers strongly endorsed these findings. Reviewer 1 states 'the authors show that overexpressed p85α(deltaExon 11) displays reduced association with the p110α catalytic subunit but strongly interacts with Irs1/2. Overexpression of PIK3R1 dominant negative mutants inhibit AKT phosphorylation and reduce cellular differentiation of preadipocytes.' Reviewer 2 confirms 'the truncated APDS2-causal p85 alpha variant impaired insulin induced signaling' and notes the findings provide 'a possible mechanistic explanation for the growing number of APDS2 patients with features of SHORT syndrome.'

result: In vitro kinase assays showed that SHORT syndrome variants (R649W, Y657X, E489K) exhibited reduced phosphotyrosine-stimulated activity in complex with p110α, p110β, and p110δ, with R649W showing the most severe loss of function. No increase in basal activity was seen for any variant.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted these biochemical findings without challenge. Reviewer 1 notes 'The authors analyze a variety of PIK3R1 mutants (i.e. deltaExon11, E489K, R649W, and Y657X), which reveals a range of phenotypes that support the proposed model for dominant negative activity.' The editor states 'conclusions are supported by a variety of mutational strategies.'

result: Co-immunoprecipitation experiments showed that the SHORT syndrome variant Y657X binds p110α, but the APDS2 ΔEx11 variant does not co-immunoprecipitate with p110α despite being detectable in lysates. This suggests the APDS2 variant does not supplant endogenous p85α binding to p110α and argues against p110α destabilization as the mechanism of dominant negative activity.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly endorsed these findings. Reviewer 1 states 'The authors convincingly show that p85α (deltaExon11, R649W, or Y657X) is unable to associate with p110α but instead more strongly associates with Irs1/2 compared to wild type p85α.' Reviewer 2 confirms 'Using immunoprecipitation of p110 alpha they did not find truncated APDS2-causal p85 alpha variant in p110 alpha precipitates.'

result: Immunoprecipitation of Irs1 (and Irs2) showed that SHORT syndrome variants R649W and Y657X reduced insulin-stimulated p110α recruitment to Irs1, while the APDS2 ΔEx11 variant abolished p110α recruitment but was itself strongly recruited to Irs1 even without insulin stimulation. This suggests ΔEx11 has preserved or enhanced ability to bind Irs1 but does not effectively compete with WT p85α for p110α binding, rendering it a more potent endogenous inhibitor than free WT p85α.
evaluation: Reviewers strongly supported these mechanistic findings. Reviewer 1 notes 'The strength of this study is the clear results derived from Western blots analysis of cell signaling markers (e.g. pAKT1), and co-immunoprecipitation of PI3K holoenzyme complexes and associated regulatory factors (e.g. Irs1/2).' Reviewer 2 confirms 'by immunoprecipitating IRS1 and IRS2 they observed that the truncated APDS2-causal p85 alpha variant was very abundant in IRS1 and IRS2 precipitates, even in the absence of insulin stimulation.'

result: The study concludes that the common APDS2 mutation produces greater hyperactivation of p110δ than p110α, while also destabilizing PI3K holoenzyme and exerting dominant negative activity on WT PIK3R1 function. These competing activating and inhibitory consequences are finely balanced and potentially differ among tissues, leading to mixed clinical profiles of gain- and loss-of-function features.
evaluation: Reviewers endorsed this overarching conclusion. The editor states 'This important study reports on PIK3R1 mutations and a paradoxical mechanism of PIK3R1 signaling' and that 'conclusions are supported by a variety of mutational strategies and cellular systems.' Reviewer 1 notes the work 'establishes a new paradigm that warrants future studies.' Reviewer 2 states the findings 'add in an interesting way possible mechanistic explanation for the growing number of APDS2 patients described with features of SHORT syndrome.'

result: The study has limitations: primary cells were studied from only a single APDS2 patient, and in the 3T3-L1 cell model, the authors did not determine whether p110δ protein could be detected.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledged these limitations. Reviewer 2 explicitly states 'The proposed paradigm is based on one cell line derived from an APDS2 patient and an overexpressing system. The investigation of a larger number of cell lines derived from APDS2 patients would further substantiate the conclusion.' Reviewer 1 notes 'Future experimentation will help reconcile the cell type specific differences (e.g. APDS2 patient derived cells vs. the 3T3-L1 cell model system) in PIK3R1 mutant behavior.'
